items.title: 66960_Gil Evans oral history interview
items.q: The interviewer quotes Ralph Gleason; Gil Evans does not respond or mention Gleason personally.

ctx.x: The whole project has been developed in cooperation with Pastor John Gensel known affectionately and wisely in New York as the priest to the jazz community. He is an associate pastor at St. Peter's Lutheran Church. And is very, very well known for his jazz projects.

Now, I'd like to quote finally from Ralph Gleason and this is on the back of the Ampex Album. He says, the thing that in a sense marks Gil Evan's work, and I'm changing the words around just a little bit here, is that he stays contemporary as do Ellington and Miles. And he draws from what is going on around him, absorbs it, digests it and when he is ready to appear again utilises it all in a new way.

I'm now going to play 'So Long'. Which is a creation as well as an arrangement of Gil Evans. This is Helen Armstead Johnston and I will not say anything more, we will simply listen to 'So Long'. Yes, I have to say one thing more and that is that this is a private memorial. That this number was really Gil's private
